messages:
incident-bot: P1 Alert — Dedicated VPC pool 'bluehollow-enterprise-01' GPU utilization >90% for 3m, queue depth rising. Possible single-tenant saturation. Auto-scaler triggered.

omar: I'm on it. Can someone grab the top-5 tenant usage and autoscaler logs? @rebecca can you pull metrics & tail the autoscaler?

rebecca: pulling now. top usage -> bluehollow-enterprise-01 = 98% GPU, queue depth 280 reqs, median wait 6.8s, p95 18s. 5xx ~1.3% (mostly 429/timeouts). I see long seq lengths and large KV cache working set for that tenant.

james: If it's a single tenant choking the pool we can enable emergency burst (spin up spare nodes) or route their traffic to less-optimized hosts. Both are workable but require customer consent for burst and exec approval for cost. @customer-ops pls confirm.

customer-ops: pinged BlueHollow via PD. They acknowledge an unexpected internal batch job kicked off and ask for immediate relief. They approve emergency burst to stabilize latency.

omar: executing burst policy: emergency-burst enable --tenant bluehollow-enterprise-01 --duration 30m --max-nodes 8

omar: ```
infractl dedicated burst enable --tenant bluehollow-enterprise-01 \
  --nodes 8 \
  --duration 30m \
  --reason "production queue spike - customer approved"
```

incident-bot: Burst request accepted; allocating 4 spare GPU nodes (policy: use spare-first). Expected ready ~120s. Tracking id: brst-20260317-42.

rebecca: applied quick throttles on batch route to limit fanout while burst comes up: `rbx route update bluehollow /batch/process --concurrency 4` — this will let interactive traffic through faster.

alexd: evicting low-priority KV prefixes to free GPU memory for inference cache: `runtime-cli cache evict --tenant bluehollow --prefix bkg-` — doing incremental evictions to avoid cache stampede.

incident-bot: Burst nodes online (4/4). Autoscaler reports effective capacity +33%. Current queue depth -> 90, median wait 1.6s, p95 3.2s, 429s now 0.2%. :white_check_mark:

james: Good. Customer reports error rate dropped and latency improved. Keep burst for 20m, then reassess. Recommend applying a soft quota and admission control to prevent repeat spikes (propose 20% over baseline for 24h).

customer-ops: BlueHollow will throttle the nightly job and follow up with an internal fix. They've requested a post-incident runbook and billing estimate for the burst.

omar: noted. Creating interim runbook and RFC for soft quotas. Handoff to night oncall @tila — please monitor the tail and escalation channel.

tila: acknowledged, will watch for regressions for next 2h and escalate if anything reappears. Please include the burst cost and timeline in the incident ticket.

rebecca: quick cost calc: 4 burst nodes * 0.5h ~= $1200 (estimate), saving interactive SLA. Adding to ticket.

incident-bot: Incident state -> MITIGATED. Create postmortem with: timeline, root cause (unintended batch job + no soft quota), mitigations performed (burst allocation, route throttling, cache eviction), follow-ups (soft quotas, alert tuning, runbook, customer billing). Assign owners in incident ticket. :spiral_notepad:

omar: closing this thread from oncall. Thanks all for quick moves. Follow-ups: rebecca -> cache eviction safeguards, james -> quota RFC, customer-ops -> confirm billing acceptance with BlueHollow.

tila: taking watch. Ping me in #incidents if anything spikes again.

incident-bot: Thread closed by oncall; SEV1 -> resolved (mitigated).
